_comment: Stage goals, the 3-star formula and the bridge-keeper quizzes for Stages 1 to 5 (FR-EVA-001, FR-EVA-002). Tuning a stage means editing this file, not GDScript. Objective types are counted by StageSession from FarmEvents: plant, water, harvest, collect_crop, till, sell_earned, buy_supply, treat_pest, grade_a, plant_tree, collect_fruit, chop_tree, harvest_seasons, sow_in_season.

evaluation._comment: score = time * weight_time + crops * weight_crops + quiz * weight_quiz. Each part is 0..1. time = par / actual (capped at 1), crops = harvested / target (capped at 1), quiz = correct / asked on the winning attempt. The bridge opens once every objective is done, which is what earns the first star.

keeper.name: Keeper Thandi
keeper.intro: Hold it! Nobody crosses my bridge without showing they know the basics.
keeper.win: Well grown! The market island is all yours.
keeper.lose: Not yet. Go look after a few more crops and come back.

questions.q: If a plant needs water to survive, what should you do to the seed right after planting it?
questions.explain: A new seed needs moist soil to start growing. Water it as soon as it is in the ground.

questions.q: Before you can plant a seed in hard ground, you must prepare the dirt. What is prepared dirt called?
questions.explain: Tilled soil is ground that has been dug and loosened, so seeds and roots can get in.

questions.q: When a crop is finished growing and ready to be picked, what do you do?
questions.explain: A ripe crop is harvested. Leave it too long and you risk losing it.

questions.q: Which farming tool is used to prepare the dirt before planting?
questions.explain: The hoe digs and loosens the ground, turning grass into a bed you can plant in.

questions.q: You plant a seed but never water it. What happens?
options: It grows normally - water does not matter
It gets stressed, gives a smaller harvest and can die
It grows faster to find water
It turns back into a seed
questions.explain: Dry soil stresses the plant. Every stressed day takes weight off the harvest, and a crop left dry long enough dies.

keeper.name: Keeper Bongani
keeper.intro: A farm is a business too. Let's see if you can count your rand.
keeper.win: Sharp! You'll need that head for numbers where pests live.
keeper.lose: Check the market prices again, then try me once more.

questions.q: When you want to sell your harvested crops to earn money, where do you go?
questions.explain: The market buys your produce. Better quality crops fetch a better price.

questions.q: What can you add to the soil to help a plant grow faster and healthier?
questions.explain: Fertiliser feeds the soil, so the crop grows faster and starts out stronger.

questions.q: What must a farmer buy from the market to start growing a brand-new crop?
questions.explain: Every crop starts from seed. Seeds cost money, so plan what you plant.

questions.q: Why do farmers need to earn and save money?
options: To buy supplies like seeds and pest treatments
To stop the seasons from changing
questions.explain: A farm is a business. Money from one harvest pays for the seeds and supplies for the next.

keeper.name: Keeper Lerato
keeper.intro: Pests don't wait for you, and neither do I. Answer quickly!
keeper.win: Your crops are in good hands. The orchard is next.
keeper.lose: The bugs won that round. Watch your plants closely and return.

questions.q: Harmful bugs and insects are eating your crops. What is this called?
questions.explain: Pests like caterpillars and worms feed on your plants. Many of them together is an infestation.

questions.q: You see worms or caterpillars damaging your plants. What should you treat them with?
options: A pest control treatment that targets them
questions.explain: Use a treatment that works on that pest. The crop info panel tells you which ones clear it.

questions.q: What happens if you let the bugs keep eating your plant?
options: A smaller harvest, or the crop is destroyed
The plant grows faster to survive
The bugs leave on their own
questions.explain: Pests do damage every day they stay. Treat them early to save your harvest.

questions.q: A crop that would have been Grade A is badly damaged by pests. What happens to its quality?
options: It turns back into a seed
It stays Grade A but stops growing
questions.explain: Damaged produce is lower quality. A crop that loses too much to pests sells as Grade B, for less money.

questions.q: Which of these is a common pest that damages crops?
questions.explain: Worms and caterpillars eat leaves and roots. Frogs and spiders actually eat pests.

keeper.name: Keeper Pieter
keeper.intro: Trees take patience. Let's see if you have some.
keeper.win: A true orchard keeper. The seasons are waiting for you.
keeper.lose: Spend a little more time among the trees, then come back.

questions.q: Apples and oranges grow on tall plants with wooden trunks. What are these called?
questions.explain: Fruit trees are planted once as a sapling and grow into a tree that bears fruit.

questions.q: An old tree is dead and blocking your farm. What removes it?
options: Chopping it down with an axe
questions.explain: The axe chops a tree down and clears the space for something new.

questions.q: How do you know a fruit tree is ready to pick?
options: You can see fruit in its leaves
The day you plant the sapling
questions.explain: A grown tree is bare for a while, then fruit appears in its leaves. That is when you pick it.

questions.q: Do fruit trees need to be replanted every time you pick their fruit?
options: No, they give fruit again and again
Yes, they die after one harvest
No, but they only fruit once ever
questions.explain: A tree keeps growing new fruit after each picking. Plant it once and it keeps giving.

questions.q: What is one disadvantage of planting a tree instead of a small ground crop?
options: It needs ten times more water
It takes up the space until you chop it down
It lowers the value of other crops
questions.explain: A tree stays where you plant it for good. Think about where it goes before you plant it.

objectives.label: Sow 3 crops that suit the season

keeper.name: Keeper Nomsa
keeper.intro: Every season has its crop. Show me you know which is which.
keeper.win: You read the seasons like a real farmer. Well done!
keeper.lose: The weather got the better of you. Watch the calendar and try again.

questions.q: Winter, spring, summer and autumn are all examples of what?
questions.explain: The year turns through four seasons, and each one suits different crops.

questions.q: A crop that needs summer heat is planted in freezing winter. What happens?
options: It sits in the ground and does not grow, and the cold damages it
It needs double the fertiliser but grows fine
questions.explain: You are allowed to plant it, but below its minimum temperature a crop stops growing and the cold hurts it. Check the season first.

questions.q: Planting different crops in a field over time to keep the soil healthy is called what?
questions.explain: Crop rotation keeps soil healthy. Beans, for example, put back nitrogen that maize uses up.

questions.q: How does a farmer know the season is about to change?
options: They get a warning before the season changes
questions.explain: A warning comes a day before each new season, so you have time to plan what to plant or harvest.

questions.q: Crops struggle in the cold. What should a farmer do before winter arrives?
options: Chop down all their fruit trees
Harvest their crops before the cold sets in
questions.explain: Winter is too cold for these crops. Bring the harvest in before it arrives, then plan for spring.
